text:
Ben Cho: Quick thread: we're revisiting the idea of a "mini-controlplane" running inside customer VPCs to reduce controlplane RTTs for high-frequency management (route updates, credential handoffs). Wanted to capture tradeoffs before I write an RFC.
Erin Zhao: Mini-CP = small agent that owns only checkout/claims and key material, not full controlplane logic, right?
Ben Cho: Exactly. It would accept signed tickets from central controlplane and expose a tiny HTTP surface to our dataplane agents. No business logic beyond auth, cert minting, and local lifecycle.
Alice Park: Main benefits I see: lower latency for route updates, fewer cross-region API calls, and better offline resilience for short blips. Also helpful for on-prem where controlplane reachability is flaky.
Carol Nguyen: Risks: increases customer trust surface. Even if tiny, the mini-CP holds secrets and needs rotation + attestation. We can't rely on the same upgrade cadence as hosted.
Ben Cho: Agreed. We were thinking of a few constraints: (1) mini-CP should only hold ephemeral keys (no long-lived secrets), (2) central controlplane issues signed time-limited tickets (JWT-style) via KMS/HSM, (3) mini-CP mints short-lived TLS certs for dataplane agents after local verification, (4) mini-CP exposes a health endpoint and a certificate revocation fetcher.
Erin Zhao: How does the handshake work when we first bootstrap? If customer network is fully private, we need an out-of-band bootstrap or operator action.
Alice Park: Bootstrapping options: 1) Operator-run installer that posts a signed bootstrap token to CP during install, 2) customer-admin uses console to generate one-time token, or 3) ephemeral out-of-band PKI enrollment (CSR flow) if customer has an internal CA.
Carol Nguyen: Another angle: instead of installing mini-CP per customer, run a regional "broker" that issues the same signed tickets but sits in the customer's transit path (peering). That keeps central trust boundary but still reduces latency. Tradeoff: regional broker adds infrastructure and cost.
Ben Cho: Good point. Broker vs mini-CP tradeoffs: Broker preserves central control; mini-CP gives best isolation and can run air-gapped.
Erin Zhao: What about revocation and compromise? If mini-CP is compromised, how do we revoke quickly? Central CP must publish revocations and force agents to re-check frequently, but that increases CP load.
Alice Park: Could use short TTLs (30s - 2m) for agent certs and a signed CRL-like digest with monotonic epoch. Agents poll epoch every 15s and refuse old tickets. Central publishes epoch increments to a global topic (pub/sub).
Carol Nguyen: That's workable but will create a lot of churn for large fleets. We need to simulate cost: number of agents * poll rate * metadata size. Also consider mobile/SDK edge where NAT timeouts affect long-polling.
Ben Cho: On the protocol surface, propose a minimal API: /claim (POST ticket), /renew (ticket), /revoke-epoch (GET), /health (GET), and /metrics. All responses signed by mini-CP's hardware-backed key. Central will verify signatures before trusting replies.
Erin Zhao: How do we protect mini-CP's identity? If it's just a keypair, we need attestation. Could integrate with cloud instance attestation (GCE/EC2 instance identity) or TPM/SGX on-prem. For BYO-hosted, rely on operator install + manual approval.
Alice Park: We should also define clear interface boundary: central CP never sends policy blobs to mini-CP. It only sends opaque tickets. Mini-CP should call back to central for policy evaluation if needed. Keep logic thin.
Carol Nguyen: Observability requirements: we need per-tenant metrics for ticket issuance latency, renew rate, last-epoch, and bootstrap failures. Also audit log events for operator actions.
Ben Cho: Ops concerns: deployment and upgrade of mini-CP across customer fleets. We must support automated upgrades with canaries and a rollback path. Also an emergency global kill-switch to force all agents to ignore mini-CP and fallback to central endpoints.
Erin Zhao: Fallback path: dataplane agents should be able to talk to either mini-CP or central CP for cert issuance. Need config precedence and a timeout for failover to avoid flapping.
Alice Park: Networking/peering impacts: mini-CP reduces cross-account egress but increases per-VPC surface we must support. For broker approach, peering counts and cross-region bandwidth cost uptick are real. Add estimated cost model to RFC.
Carol Nguyen: Security doc note: document accepted threat model (insider at customer, compromised mini-CP host, MITM between CP and mini-CP). Define mitigations (short TTL, mandatory signed response verification, attestation).
Ben Cho: For rollout plan, propose alpha with internal beta customers who can tolerate staged deploys. Include a lab that simulates intermittent central CP connectivity, attestation failures, and epoch roll increments.
Erin Zhao: Testing: build a chaos job that kills central CP connectivity, rotates epoch, and validates agents reacquire certs from mini-CP or fallback to central. Also exercise operator rollback.
Alice Park: I can draft the RFC with proposed API, bootstrap flows, revocation mechanics, and rollout checklist. Will include metrics and cost modeling sections.
Carol Nguyen: Please include a short appendix on migration from current model (all-central) to hybrid. Also call out long-term refactor: replace mini-CP with regional brokers if we can't operationalize per-customer installs.
infra-bot: Note: plan created "mini-CP-exploratory" and assigned to infra-eng.
Ben Cho: Thanks. Ping me when draft is ready; I'll add the network cost estimates and security review owner.
